subject: Compact session quantum & billing reconciliation
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.z@nimblecart.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected charges for compact sessions

Hi Rachel —

Hope you’re well. Our infra team spotted a jump in the May invoice and after a quick look it appears the largest contributor is a new line item labelled "compact-session quantum charges". We see a lot of short calls from our product assistants (median request ~35 tokens, typical context <512) but the bill seems to reflect a much larger per-call unit.

Quick background: we added a small edge feature last month that performs many single-turn rule checks (90–120k calls/day) — each call is tiny and stateless. Historically we expected these to be covered under our existing commit, but the invoice shows almost 60% of May overage mapped to these compact sessions.

Can you explain how compact sessions are being metered? Specifically:
- What is the minimum quantum for a single request (tokens)?
- Is there rounding per-call or per-minute/window?
- Do short, repeated calls from the same user/context share any prefix or KV cache credit that reduces charging?

I attached a sample invoice excerpt (sample-invoice.pdf) and a CSV we exported from our side. We’re trying to reconcile quickly because this impacts our forecast and a pending capacity commit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

—Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of ML Platforms, NimbleCart
emily.z@nimblecart.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: sample-invoice.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.z@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges for compact sessions

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the invoice excerpt. We pulled the account history and I wanted to share some quick context and an initial reconciliation so you have something to work with immediately. I’m attaching a short calculation sheet (billing-calc.xlsx) that mirrors what we ran.

Short answers up front:
- Minimum quantum: for the SKU you’re on, the metering quantum is 256 tokens. That means any call that consumes <=256 billable tokens is rounded up to 256 for metering purposes.
- Rounding cadence: rounding happens at the request level (per call). We don’t aggregate multiple discrete requests into a single quantum unless they are part of the same pinned session or streaming session.
- Prefix/KV reuse: automatic KV cache reuse can reduce compute but does not retroactively reduce the minimum per-request quantum. Prefetch/pinned sessions (long-lived) can share a KV that avoids recomputation and therefore reduces billable tokens, but for short stateless calls each request will hit the quantum floor.

Example (from the attached sheet):
- Typical call tokens (prompt + expected completion): ~40 tokens => billed as 256 tokens per call
- 100k calls/day at that pattern => effective billed tokens ~25.6M tokens/day instead of 4M tokens if counted at actual token usage.

Two follow-ups I need from you to finalize the line-item reconciliation:
1) Can you confirm whether those 90–120k calls/day are being opened as individual short REST requests (stateless) vs. a background streaming connection or pinned session? If you can share a short sample call trace (headers + whether session_id present) that’d help.
2) Do you want us to reprocess May with a one-time revision to map any identified pinned/streaming sessions (if present) to shared-session accounting? We can do a one-off reclass and propose a credit if there was a misclassification.

As a mitigation option, if you expect continued high-volume short calls we can recommend one of two paths:
- Short-term: enable our microbatching gateway (client-side change) that will batch small calls over a 1s window and significantly reduce per-call quantum impact.
- Long-term: consider a low-latency reserved capacity commit for the compact-session workload; that would change your effective unit cost and remove strict per-request quantum rounding.

I’ll leave Vanessa and Ben on copy — they own billing policy and pilot concessions for usage patterns like this. If you’d like, we can set up a 30-minute reconciliation call later today or tomorrow.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Billing, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Attachment: billing-calc.xlsx (XLSX, 14 KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges for compact sessions

Rachel / Ben —

Looping back after reviewing Emily’s sample invoice and our logs for NimbleCart. Summary of findings and proposed customer-facing resolution below. (I also drafted a short credit note for approval — proposed-credit-note.pdf).

Findings:
- Confirmed: the account generated ~3.5M discrete short requests during May that were stateless REST calls (no session_id header), which per our policy get rounded to the 256-token quantum.
- Where it matters: ~72% of those calls averaged <70 tokens, so the quantum overhead explains the majority of the surprise in their overage line.
- No evidence of pinned/persistent sessions for that workload in our telemetry.

Proposed resolution (triage + longer-term):
1) One-time credit: offer a retrospective credit that refunds 50% of the quantum-overhead charge for May (we calculate ~$18,400 credit). This is a goodwill concession given the unexpected billing impact and NimbleCart’s growth trajectory.
2) Technical mitigation: share the microbatching SDK snippet and help them enable the 1s gateway in a pilot window — we expect 60–80% reduction in billed tokens for this pattern.
3) Commercial option: if they will commit to a 12-month low-latency reserved pool sized to their compact sessions (proposal attached as an addendum), we’ll convert the remaining overage exposure to discounted per-token rates and eliminate per-call quantum rounding for requests routed through the reserved pool.

If you agree we should propose this to Emily as a combined package (credit + microbatch pilot + commit option). Ben — can you confirm the credit number in the sheet matches accounting’s allowed concession ceiling? Also confirm whether we need a one-time approval from finance for the $18.4k.

Emily — if that sounds reasonable we can send a short note outlining the credit and the microbatching steps. We can also schedule a technical touchpoint this week to walk their infra team through the SDK changes.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success & Billing, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed-credit-note.pdf (PDF, 6 KB)
